summary: Practise USAID award budgeting, cost review, cash forecasting, subrecipient monitoring, and financial reporting. Explore the five-day course outline.
lede: Financial management for funded projects connects approved budgets, transaction records, payment approvals and reporting evidence to support oversight of award resources. For finance officers, grants managers, project accountants and project leads, the course develops practical skills in budget-to-account mapping, cost documentation, cash forecasting, reconciliations and subrecipient monitoring, with exercises on financial report evidence and closeout decisions.
audienceIntro: This foundation course suits professionals who prepare, review, or approve financial records for USAID-funded awards and need a clearer connection between award terms, project transactions, and reporting evidence.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with project budgets or bookkeeping is helpful. No programming is required. Bring a laptop with Excel installed.
topics: Financial management for NGOs & donor-funded projects
